sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is Surprisingly More Different Than You Think | IGN Preview
sources.text: Taking my first steps out of Link’s treehouse and into Kokiri Forest, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake came to life. Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma described this as a “faithful interpretation” of the Nintendo 64 original , and that term stuck with me as I explored Hyrule for more than an hour. This is far from a 1:1 remake: I found familiar rooms containing redesigned challenges that change how the world and player function. I spoke to old friends who had new things to say that added texture to Hyrule and its people. And, I unpacked how its updated controls and detailed art design redefine its old-school combat and puzzle solving for the modern day. This remake isn’t about scope; it’s about depth. The Zelda series is full of old stories, and the Ocarina of Time remake presents itself as a legend retold, with clear theatrical inspirations that have completely changed how I’m approaching it. First, a quick word about spoilers. I know some of you have never played the N64 game, meaning Ocarina of Time will be a wholly new experience. So, I’m only going to talk about explicitly what I saw in the three chunks I played during the preview. Two sections were split across the first 90-ish minutes of the adventure, while the third and largest section was set in the first dungeon you play as Adult Link, which happens at roughly the one-third mark of the story. So, there will be no spoilers for anything outside of what Nintendo chose to show us. Back to Kokiri Forest. Not counting last-gen upgrades or spinoffs, this is the series’ proper Nintendo Switch 2 debut, and the leap forward in quality immediately drew me in. Rays of light poke through the trees; moss and mushrooms thrive on the withered bark; our hero’s tunic is decorated with handwoven flourishes – and it’s all running at a crisp 60 fps. A pleasant musical performance recreates the forest’s original MIDI theme with what sounds like just a handful of real musicians. Hyrule has never felt more intimately realized than this. That applies to the dialogue as well. Later, a Castle Town citizen gawks at Link’s outfit, treating him as some foreign outsider from the distant forest: “Intricate stitching that implies the whole ensemble is handmade!” he excitedly says. The forest’s shopkeeper apologizes to Link for his empty shelves, blaming the stubborn Kokiri ringleader Mido for blocking the path to the Great Deku Tree, where the staff goes to restock. No matter how hard I try to juke Mido, he won’t let anyone pass without a sword and a shield. Here, the remake shows its willingness to change up Ocarina’s level design. After crawling to the secret area that contains the Kokiri Sword, I find that the challenge to reach it has been overhauled. The treasure chest used to be tucked away in the back corner of a maze with a giant boulder – now it’s perched on a high platform in the center of the room, with the boulder rolling around it. The fact that it’s different is interesting on its own, but the way this change impacts what this room is now asking of you reveals a lot. On N64, this obstacle was about learning to recenter the camera behind Link by tapping Z to see around corners and avoid the boulder. It was teaching you how to play one of the first 3D action-adventure games ever made. This remake no longer carries that burden, and that lesson is unnecessary since the right stick provides complete camera control. Instead, since Link can now jump at the press of a button, this room marks the first time you are required to jump in order to reach the treasure. It stripped out an obsolete tutorial and replaced it with a newly relevant one. My hour in Ocarina was stuffed with nuanced differences like this. I’m fully equipped now that I have the sword and shield, and Link feels excellent to control. His movement felt immediately familiar to Link in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, with a dash, a jump, and snappy third-person gyro aiming with projectile-based weapons like the slingshot. I was running, leaping, and sniping spiders like a pro in the first dungeon, Inside the Great Deku Tree. I worked my way to the area I was most looking forward to seeing. Ever since Aonuma’s gameplay demonstration, I’ve been interested in Ocarina’s apparent fascination with a more logically constructed world . As seen in one room of Inside the Great Deku Tree, a floating platform from the N64 game has been replaced by a crumbling bridge that’s now actually built into the environment. I came in with the idea that the remake cares about explaining every element of its world, and my preview session only reinforced that theory. I was on the lookout for more instances of this in the Forest Temple. Atmospheric fog blankets the ground in this old, haunted mansion where Adult Link hunts down four ghosts. After two open-world 3D Zeldas that largely took a break from the franchise’s traditional dungeons, it felt great to push blocks around, navigate through twisted hallways, and collect small keys. I was reminded of how classic Zelda design welcomes different types of logic and reasoning than Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom’s open-ended approach. While the Forest Temple’s overall layout was mostly unchanged, it included new cutscenes that fleshed out the dungeon’s antagonists, and yet again showed differences in how specific moments played out. An arena where Link fights a Stalfos used to have a giant hole in the middle. Link needed to avoid it or risk falling to the floor below, but the Stalfos could defy gravity and hover over the gap. You could explain it away as part of this dungeon’s supernatural trickery, but it always looked out of place to me. Here, that hole has been exchanged for a shallow pool of acid. The skeleton enemies can still walk in it – they don’t have any flesh to lose – while Link takes damage if he enters it. This means the fight plays out the same as it used to: the Stalfos has access to the whole room while Link is constrai

sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's infamous tutorial owl seemingly won't trap you in conversation in the Switch 2 remake
sources.text: It looks like the owl known Kaepora Gaebora - part-tutorial, part-tip giver - will be far less talkative in the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . Who is the most dangerous monster you face in Ocarina of Time ? 'Ganondorf' you'll surely answer. Wrong. 'Koume and Kotake', you might offer. After all, they raised Ganondorf and set him down his evil path. Incorrect. 'Okay, then it must be the Shadow Temple boss, the dastardly Bongo Bongo'. You fool. The most vicious villain can only be Kaepora Gaebora, the owl. Sure, he appears helpful. Some might even say he's secretly Rauru, Sage of Light, but show me the evidence! (So I can ignore it). You might even use the lift he offers down Death Mountain to excuse his overly long explanations, but, never forget, always beware owls bearing free flights. Seriously, think about it. What's the best, sneakiest, way to slow down the Hero of Time? A monster ambush? You can easily slay those beasts with a few sword slashes. But being captured in a one-sided conversation… one that forces you to slam the A button - because you already know how the map works and definitely know where you're going - only to suddenly be asked whether you want to hear all of that guff again… Of course you don't. Who would? But you've already hit A so you're going to hear it again and again and again. Slowly the edges of your soul begin to tatter and, with every loose thread, your desire to escape wanes until you simply give up. All that remains is one very smug owl. I know I'm not the only person that's been trapped in an endless circle of 'Did you get all that?' at the behest of this cursed avian. But it seems our collective suffering is at an end. During my preview of the Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake, I was very, very, worried about meeting the owl. I only had 15 minutes to explore both Hyrule Field and Hyrule Castle Town. A small amount of time which could easily get cut even shorter if I made one bad decision. I could feel Kaepora Gaebora circling above me as if I was a field mouse and he, well, an owl. When the time came, I took a deep breath. I would pay attention. I would not fall for his 'yes means no, no means yes' trap. Not this time. Yet the damned owl surprised me: the conversation was short. Pleasant even. Not a single mention of the map was made and, before I knew it, the owl was flying away. I can't say whether the owl's incessant talking has been cut down in other points in the game, but it would track with the other quality-of-life changes made to Ocarina of Time in this remake. (There's an Ocarina of Time preview waiting for you if you'd like to learn more. Nudge, nudge, wink, wink.) What we do know is that he's been fitted with a new design and, thanks to the game's trailer, will still offer flights from Lake Hylia. For now, we'll just have to wait until the remake is released on 5th November to learn exactly how talkative the owl actually is.

sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: The Ocarina of Time remake feels remarkably modern — and surprisingly terrifying
sources.text: New tech and gameplay improvements make it easier to get into Nintendo’s defining title. New tech and gameplay improvements make it easier to get into Nintendo’s defining title. With its upcoming remake for the Switch 2, Nintendo might have nailed the best thing about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time : its timelessness. The 1998 3D action adventure game for the Nintendo 64 that pioneered so much — 3D graphics, movement, exploration, openness — has been reengineered with changes that make it feel more modern, and surprisingly terrifying at times. Based on my early hands-on time with the game, it’s shaping up to be the best-looking, best-playing version of the game that addresses the most frustrating aspects of playing the original. More than just sanding off its roughest edges, Nintendo also fitted Ocarina of Time with modern trappings to make it more welcoming to those who were introduced to Zelda through more modern releases, like Breath of the Wild . The remake has a new progression marker, called Threads of Time, that’s viewable when you pause. It also has Zelda Notes integration within the Nintendo Switch app to let you view game maps and other info on your phone. Oh, it also has a dedicated jump button. I spent around 90 minutes during a recent preview event in New York City playing through some chunks of the game, including when you first take control of Child Link, and later on after you yank the Master Sword in the Temple of Time to become Adult Link. Its story still makes it a standout Zelda title, and the improvements make it even easier to get immersed in. In some ways, the remake feels similar to modern Zelda games. Link is snappy to control, and lock-on combat is engaging. Swapping between items and weapons no longer requires hopping into the pause menu, as it did in the original. Holding a shoulder button halts the action, and you can navigate with an analog stick to find what you want in near-realtime. However, it’s an adventure on a much smaller scale; the complexity of your quests, and the tools at your disposal for combat and getting around are simpler, but no less fun. All of the sections I played were truncated, though I left feeling confident that Nintendo nailed this remake. My favorite section was the Forest Temple, which really shows off the more realistic art style. It can finally portray the game’s horror themes in ways that weren’t possible 28 years ago. For example, Link traverses rooms in the dungeon that have red stained glass windows, and as he passes through beams of light, he is cast in the color of blood. It really looks and feels like he’s on an adventure to stave off cataclysm, and the visual evolution frequently made me stop playing for a second while I took in the changes. Also, being able to use the right stick to control the camera lets you create cinematic moments on-the-fly, which is great if, like me, you like taking a lot of screenshots. Ocarina of Time is one of Nintendo’s most influential games, and playing it is a rite of passage for any Zelda fan, but it can be tough to go back to the original. As accessible as it is considering it was one of Nintendo’s earliest fully-3D titles, the remake makes it so much easier to get into. And it’s launching at a time when the Zelda franchise is bigger than ever. Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom were big sellers, and they continue to attract new players years after launch, while fans will be able to dig into the live-action movie in April 2027 . Even sooner, though, Switch 2 owners will get to feast on the best way to play through a defining Zelda classic. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launches for the Nintendo Switch 2 on Thursday, November 5th.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Preview
sources.text: Nintendo’s new version of a Zelda classic is sharp, streamlined, and plays better than ever Remaking The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a tricky needle for Nintendo to thread. The Nintendo Switch 2 update of the Nintendo 64 classic needs to feel both authentic to the original, groundbreaking game while somehow feeling of a piece with modern Zelda titles, such as Breath of the Wild . After spending roughly 30 minutes playing November’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , Nintendo seems to have pulled it off. The remake is both incredibly impressive graphically and the game now plays better than ever. The remake evokes nostalgia for Link’s first 3D adventure while also feeling thoroughly modern. My hands-on time with the game covered much of what series producer Eiji Aonuma showed in his gameplay demonstration during a Nintendo Direct showcase in September. I started at the very beginning of the game, when Link earns his new fairy, Navi, and visits the Great Deku Tree to explore his first dungeon. From there, I strolled through Hyrule Field and into its bustling Castle Town. Later, I explored a heretofore unseen section of the Ocarina of Time remake, the twisting, turning Forest Temple. One impression of the remake remained consistent throughout my hands-on time: Nintendo’s new Zelda is snappy, streamlined, and polished in ways that make it feel totally fresh. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 starts in a familiar way. Navi the fairy is tasked with waking the fairyless boy Link, conveying a message from the wise old Deku Tree. In this opening section, I relearned the basics of interaction and combat. I visited my Kokiri friends for conversation and learned what I need to progress. That included acquiring a Kokiri sword, earned by visiting a nook in the forest, and earning enough rupees to purchase a Deku shield. These activities, which taught me to jump — yes, Link can manually jump now, using either the X or B button on a Joy-Con 2 controller — and pick up and throw objects, felt speedy and precise. I feel like I blitzed through the opening tutorials, confronting the bossy Mido with such efficiency that even he must have been impressed. After speaking to the gorgeously rendered Great Deku Tree, I ventured inside with Link to explore the interior dungeon. Here too, combat against Skulltulas and Deku Baba felt incredibly responsive. Ocarina of Time controls like a dream on Switch 2, and as I acquired items like the Fairy Slingshot and Link’s bow and arrow, swapping between secondary weapons and items was speedy using the R button to cycle through his inventory. One more thing stood out to me during my limited time in the Deku Tree: Gold Skulltula Tokens look absolutely beautiful. Nintendo’s rendering of textures and light in the Ocarina of Time remake is unlike anything else I’ve seen on Switch 2. After exploring the Great Deku Tree, I was visited by the owl Kaepora Gaebora, who directed me to Hyrule Castle. Here, I got a look at the new Threads of Time feature that Nintendo is adding to the Ocarina of Time remake. In the game’s main menu, I could check in on a log of Link’s adventure thus far, reminding myself of key story beats and checking on my next destination. It’s a bit of new hand-holding, but also a handy way to reacquaint oneself with the narrative’s current state. Hyrule Field is vast . You can see landmarks like Hyrule Castle and Death Mountain in the far-off distance, and the walk to the nearby Castle Town feels initially a bit daunting. But Link can now dash, making traversing long distances much quicker. I did make one diversion in Hyrule Field, taking down a large Peahat near the town’s drawbridge, just to get a better handle on combat against a tougher enemy. Inside Hyrule Castle Town, the area is teeming with life. Townspeople move to and fro, engaging in dance and conversation. Engaging them in chatter and finding side-quest opportunities felt immediately distracting in my first visit to the remake’s town. I can’t wait to revisit it when I have more time. After spending some time playing as Young Link in the early portions of the game, I loaded up a save that featured a playable Adult Link. At this point in the game, Link has the Hook Shoot, a tool that’s key to exploring the Forest Temple, one of Ocarina of Time ’s most memorable dungeons. It was in the Forest Temple that I started to fully appreciate the streamlined movement and combat in the remake, as well as the attention to detail in breathing new life into old spaces. The Forest Temple looks gorgeous. It feels tangible and ancient, with vines and moss laying its stone walls. Small adjustments to the temple’s architecture make the space feel real, while staying true to the soul of the original. Each quadrant feels distinct, thanks to improved lighting and textures. Small environmental touches, like an ever-present mist flowing along the floors, give the space an ethereal mood. It’s a gorgeous space to play in. But even with the game’s speedy movement and controls, I was unable to meet the dungeon’s boss, Phantom Ganon, during the time limit I was under. But after exploring the Forest Temple’s twisting hallways and clever puzzles, I was intoxicated. I can’t wait to revisit this place and see how the rest of the game has evolved when Nintendo's new The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time finally arrives. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released on Nov. 5, exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake ‘Overview’ trailer
sources.text: Nintendo has released a five-minute overview trailer for the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . Here is an overview of the game, via Nintendo: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Invites you to put yourself at the center of an epic adventure as you join Link on a journey of growth and discovery through the kingdom of Hyrule. Together with a guiding fairy named Navi, you’ll encounter lively characters, battle ferocious monsters and use cunning to overcome obstacles in search of the mythical Triforce—and to save Hyrule from falling into darkness! The key to this adventure lies with the ocarina, with its powerful melodies that are able to stir space and time and lead Link toward a new destiny. In this completely reborn version of the game, you’ll be able to bring some of the ocarina magic into your real world. Hum a melody Link has learned or even play one on an actual instrument, and the Nintendo Switch 2 microphone will hear your song and cause Link’s ocarina in the game to respond! This reborn version also introduces the Hall of Fallen Heroes, a place where statues of defeated monsters reside. Venture there to learn about them or engage them in a rematch battle! This new version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time also features overhauled visuals, fully voiced cutscenes with expanded dialogue, and full symphonic orchestral music! The game also supports ZELDA NOTES , a service available within the Nintendo Switch App for compatible smart devices that allows you to get even more out of your adventure. There will also be two new The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time amiibo figures launching in 2027, which unlock special in-game masks—existing amiibo figures from the Legend of Zelda series will also provide useful rewards when tapped during gameplay! Celebrate the 40th anniversary of the original Legend of Zelda game with this immersive adventure where you can be introduced—or reintroduced—to this magical world and become the Hero of Time to save Hyrule from the forces of darkness! The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is due out for Switch 2 on November 5.

sources.title: A atualização Spec IV (Parte 1) de Gran Turismo 7 é lançada hoje e uma prévia do controle sem fio DualSense – Edição Limitada Gran Turismo
sources.text: A atualização mais recente inclui o lendário Sugo Circuit, seis novos veículos e mais formas de vivenciar sua paixão por dirigir. Olá a todos, estamos empolgados em compartilhar novidades sobre Gran Turismo com vocês hoje. Para começar, temos todos os detalhes da Parte 1 da atualização Spec IV de Gran Turismo 7 , que chega hoje. Além disso, celebramos os 30 anos de Gran Turismo com uma prévia do controle sem fio DualSense Edição Limitada Gran Turismo! Continue lendo e saiba todos os detalhes. Hoje, todos os jogadores receberão a Parte 1 da atualização Spec IV de Gran Turismo 7. Se você gosta de buscar tempos de volta, descobrir a história automotiva, tirar a foto perfeita, montar a coleção dos seus sonhos ou simplesmente busca algo novo para pilotar, a Spec IV adiciona novas formas de explorar o mundo dos carros com seis novos veículos, o circuito Sportsland Sugo, novos eventos, locais do Scapes, recursos de jogabilidade e muito mais. Esta atualização também traz novos recursos de Visualização de Carros, modo Experiência, 6 novos eventos de Circuitos Mundiais e muito mais! Tudo isso estará disponível gratuitamente a partir de hoje, 16 de outubro, às 3h BRT*. O Xiaomi Vision Gran Turismo é um hipercarro elétrico esculpido pelo vento. Seu cockpit em formato de lágrima está integrado em uma carroceria esculpida com recortes e dutos de ar, formando canais aerodinâmicos por todo o veículo. A lanterna traseira em formato de halo serve tanto como um ícone visual quanto como uma enorme saída de ar. Junto com inovações como o Active Wake Control System e os Accretion Rims, o carro atinge um coeficiente de arrasto de 0,29, força descendente de -1,2 e uma classificação de eficiência aerodinâmica de 4,1 por meio de testes simulados iterativos, alcançando novos níveis de equilíbrio entre baixo arrasto e alta força descendente para hipercarros elétricos. “Os hipercarros elétricos precisam responder a uma pergunta fundamental”, disse Tianyuan Li, Chefe de Design da Xiaomi Auto. “Buscamos um arrasto extremamente baixo para velocidade em linha reta ou força descendente máxima para superar curvas? A solução ideal é encontrar o equilíbrio perfeito entre os dois.” Essa abordagem impressionou o produtor da série Gran Turismo Kazunori Yamauchi. “Quando vi que a Xiaomi tinha resolvido a contradição entre baixo arrasto e alta força descendente, fiquei realmente maravilhado.” Experimente isto em GT7: leve-o ao circuito de Spa-Francorchamps no evento Troféu Vision Gran Turismo e veja como seu design futurista funciona em um dos circuitos mais históricos do automobilismo. A Ferrari, a marca do cavalo empinado, sediada em Maranello, na Itália, elevou os carros ao reino da arte, colocando tecnologia e paixão das pistas de corrida em seus carros de produção. Um carro que dá continuidade à linhagem de seus carros esportivos de motor central é a F355 Berlinetta de 1994. A carroceria da Pininfarina é uma obra-prima que combina lindas curvas e beleza funcional. As linhas quadradas da 348 evoluíram muito, equilibrando desempenho aerodinâmico e beleza sensual em um alto nível. Só olhar para o carro faz seu coração bater mais rápido. É a aparência de uma verdadeira Ferrari. Experimente isto em GT7: vá para o circuito Sportsland Sugo e deixe o equilíbrio e a capacidade de resposta da Ferrari ganharem vida nas curvas fluidas e nas mudanças de elevação do circuito. O Mugen Motul Civic, que conquistou a vitória geral na categoria no All-Japan Touring Car Championship de 1987, foi um carro de corrida do Grupo A desenvolvido a partir do modelo “Si” de duplo came que entrou para a linha de 3ª geração do Civic em 1984. A versão do Grupo A do Civic Si presente em Gran Turismo é baseada nesse Mugen Motul Civic. O Si, o primeiro carro de produção da Honda em 20 anos a ser equipado com um motor DOHC, demonstrou seu alto desempenho até mesmo como um carro de produção e era perfeito para o Grupo A. A Mugen desenvolveu o carro ainda mais e amadureceu a plataforma em corridas antes de fornecer peças para equipes privadas. Experimente isto em GT7: participe de um dos novos eventos de Copa dos Amadores e veja se consegue manter o ritmo em cada curva como o carro de corrida original fazia. A Mazda continuou a aperfeiçoar a linhagem de motores rotativos desde que seu “Cosmo Sport” foi lançado em 1967. O “GT3 CONCEPT” foi um carro de corrida que trouxe de volta o motor de 4 rotores que mantém a filosofia do 787B, um carro que venceu Le Mans, combinando-o com a mais recente tecnologia SKYACTIV. Esta linda fera foi refinada ainda mais e evoluiu para batalhas árduas e competição nas pistas. Experimente isto em GT7: leve-o para um evento de Mundial de Turismo e aprenda como cada ajuste e cada ápice podem reduzir um tempo precioso em uma volta. Desde sua primeira aparição em 1996, o Step WGN (pronunciado como “step wagon”) sempre foi uma minivan popular com as famílias devido ao seu grande espaço interno, forma quadrada e proposta utilitária, incluindo o piso baixo e as grandes portas deslizantes. Na linha, o “Spada” recebeu uma grade dianteira ampla e robusta, e a moldura cromada que envolve a parte inferior da carroceria confere uma sensação de poder e classe. O “Spada Premium Line” vai além com detalhes cromados de platina especiais. Este é um modelo de classe superior que garante aos passageiros uma experiência sublime tanto em trajetos diários quanto em longas viagens. Experimente isto em GT7: coloque-o no Scapes e descubra como um veículo familiar pode ser fotogênico diante de alguns dos locais mais bonitos de Gran Turismo. O Citroën 2 CV é uma obra-prima do carro do povo francês, produzido por 42 anos desde o lançamento em 1948. Seu design é tão simples que foi chamado de um guarda-chuva com rodas, mas ele veio com uma suspensão flexível que permitia carregar ovos sem quebrá-los em qualquer tipo de terreno acidentado, um interior amplo que permitia o uso em viagens longas e um preço que o tornava acessível para qualquer pessoa. stories.title: Epic Games reportedly delays Star Wars and Marvel shooter, as the Fortnite maker embraces "AI-accelerated development"
stories.summary: Epic Games has reportedly turned to gen-AI to finish up development on a shooter that crosses over Star Wars and Marvel, which has been internally delayed. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Epic Games reportedly delays Star Wars and Marvel shooter, as the Fortnite maker embraces "AI-accelerated development"
sources.text: Epic Games has reportedly turned to gen-AI to finish up development on a shooter that crosses over Star Wars and Marvel, which has been internally delayed. That's according to a Bloomberg report from journalist Jason Schreier, citing anonymous sources familiar with the unannounced game. Epic's in-development project - a collaboration with Disney - is said to have hit a speed bump, and the Fortnite maker is apparently telling its developers to embrace more gen-AI tools for the rest of the game's production. The new shooter purportedly features characters from both the Marvel and Star Wars series, and the company expected to have it out the door in March 2027. Now that the crossover project has slipped, Epic reportedly told its staff to adopt an "AI first" production pipeline and finish the game with tech such as Anthropic's Claude. In an internal message seen by Bloomberg, one game director told developers there would be "no more hand-written code" and art work should be "generated with full AI workflows" - much to the surprise of many workers. "We're embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," Epic's communications director, Jake Jones, said in a statement to Bloomberg. "We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration," CEO Tim Sweeney tweeted . "The aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal." The Walt Disney company acquired a $1.5b stake in Epic Games a few years back, as the two entertainment giants agreed to partner on a "games and entertainment universe" somehow connected to Fortnite. There weren't any concrete details on the collaboration at the time, though the duo said players would be able to "create their own stories and experiences, express their fandom in a distinctly Disney way, and share content with each other in ways that they love". More recently, it was reported that senior Disney executives were interested in buying Epic Games outright . Epic's push for gen-AI to infiltrate almost all levels of game development comes less than a year after it laid off over 1,000 humans . At the time, CEO Tim Sweeney told staff "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded."

sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: Epic is bringing Fortnite to Linux
sources.text: There’s no timeline on when, but Epic is rebuilding its anti-cheat software so that Fortnite will be playable on Linux. There’s no timeline on when, but Epic is rebuilding its anti-cheat software so that Fortnite will be playable on Linux. Epic is working on bringing Fortnite to Linux through its Epic Games Launcher. The new launcher is releasing in preview today, and for the first time on Linux, and while Fortnite isn’t available there just yet, Epic wants to make that a reality. So far, part of the reason Fortnite hasn’t been available on Linux is concerns about cheating. While Epic’s Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) service does support Linux, Fortnite itself does not, and in February 2022, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney said that for Fortnite , “We don’t have confidence that we’d be able to combat cheating at scale under a wide array of kernel configurations.” But now, Epic says it’s planning to rebuild EAC for Linux, which it is calling EAC Linux v2. “To bring Fortnite to Linux, we are rebuilding Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) and working with distro maintainers on security requirements,” Epic says in a blog post . “Once it’s working with a critical mass of distro maintainers, we’ll bring Fortnite to Linux via the Epic Games Launcher. We’ll also make these improvements available to other developers so they can bring their games to Linux players.” Epic plans to pilot EAC Linux v2 in Fortnite first, Epic says in a separate post focused on the anti-cheat update. The company doesn’t have a timeline for when the Fortnite Linux version might be available, Epic engineering director Rick Deist tells The Verge in a briefing. Epic is also “investigating” making the game compatible with Valve’s Linux-based SteamOS, Deist says, though the company does not plan to bring Fortnite to Valve’s Steam store, according to Epic Games Store VP and GM Martin Keely. The company also says that the Steam Deck “does not support the required features for our EAC v2 solution, but we are actively talking with Valve and hope to support it in the future.”

stories.title: "I was forced to ship the game" - Glen Schofield blames Krafton management for The Callisto Protocol's problems
stories.summary: Glen Schofield, the game-maker best known for co-creating Dead Space, has blamed Korean company Krafton - the owner of PUBG - for the shortcomings of his horror game successor The Callisto Protocol , which it published. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: "I was forced to ship the game" - Glen Schofield blames Krafton management for The Callisto Protocol's problems
sources.text: "A lot of them were caused by Korean management." Glen Schofield, the game-maker best known for co-creating Dead Space, has blamed Korean company Krafton - the owner of PUBG - for the shortcomings of his horror game successor The Callisto Protocol , which it published. In an interview with GamesIndustry.biz , Schofield expressed frustrated bewilderment at Krafton's handling of his Striking Distance company, which it had invested in, during the Covid pandemic. Krafton allegedly promised Striking Distance three extra months of development time and then rescinded it. "I was forced to ship the game," Schofield said. "I'm mad at myself, there's no doubt. I was so stunned by that decision, because we had fucking Covid. A million people died in America. I lost one of my best friends. "Every single month, four to six people in my company were getting sick. There were times [when] our small team in Spain was shut down; it goes through a small place like that and you lose your rendering team for a while. "The main thing you're concerned about, not that you aren't normally, is the health of your team. Making a game just became secondary because this is about life. This is about humanity." Schofield has discussed the decision to deny the three extra months of development time before . Had it not, then The Callisto Protocol would have been released in March 2023, rather than December 2022. This sudden rug-pull had also come after years of the studio adapting to working during a pandemic already, which Schofield said had been very hard to do. "When you have a studio of a hundred people, you can touch a hundred people a day. When they're at home, you have to do individual calls, or I could get everybody together on Zoom," said Schofield. "But we did it. We did all these things because we were searching for the best way to do it. There were so many meetings. "We had to learn on the job and just change everything," he added. "We got it done and everything. We saw the problems that we had. A lot of them were caused by Korean management." Before it was embroiled in a legal battle with Subnautica 2 creators , Krafton was mostly known as the PUBG company. Having found so much success with the battle royale shooter and its off-shoots, the publisher was ready to invest in the triple-A space - but it seemingly wasn't ready for that new role. Schofield said Krafton lacked the necessary experience to release a single-player physical game, forcing Striking Distance to build an internal team to do that. Krafton also allegedly mandated a release of The Callisto Protocol on PlayStation 4 alongside PS5, which would cost "another $20 million", Schofield said, and require sending out 200 dev kits to developers during a global chip shortage. None of that helped The Callisto Protocol's fortunes, and Krafton wasn't happy with its financial performance as a result. "[Krafton] thought Callisto was a complete failure," Schofield revealed. "What they didn't know while all they were doing was complaining, we were doing patches. I waited until I finished all the DLC and put out 86 patches. That was a lot of fucking work. Every day you're going in, you're making changes. Some are little, others are massive. That was all to get it back to where it needed to be." The Callisto Protocol received a mixed reception at launch, owing to technical and performance issues but also to core design elements relating to combat. In the Eurogamer review of The Callisto Protocol , Vikki Blake praised the game's production values but lamented its lack of depth and tension compared to Dead Space.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: GTA 3's iconic box art was changed at the last minute because of 9/11, ex-Rockstar lead Dan Houser reveals
sources.text: Dan Houser, one of Rockstar's co-founders that left the GTA 6 studio in 2020 , has given a wide-ranging new interview with IGN, covering topics including the tortured production of Bully , changes made to Grand Theft Auto 3's artwork post-9/11, the reaction to Red Dead Redemption's ending , and why he thinks Max Payne 3 was a failure . The most interesting to me is how the iconic boxart for GTA 3 - a template that has been used for every game since, by the way, most recently being co-opted for GTA 6's cover - was actually put together very last minute. "What's funny is the cover art that became the iconic GTA cover art; Stephen Bliss did that in about two evenings because the old cover art was probably being too offensive to release after 9/11 because there were burning buildings in it," Houser revealed to IGN . "So it would've been fine if there hadn't just been 9/11. So that look of the shards, the squares that became very iconic, only appeared because of 9/11." GTA 3 takes place in Liberty City - a thinly-veiled parody of the real-world New York City, where the 9/11 disaster, of course, took place. So there was sensitivity around showing destruction and death publicly in the months and years after. This is something that Rockstar had to consider carefully as it was launching the game into the aftermath of the event. "There were a couple of bits of content that would've been fine, but in the exact aftermath of 9/11, were maybe a little bit too much," Houser explained. "So we had to take those out, and the team [rallied] round and remove those and edit a couple of lines of dialogue and did a quick content stand and thought it was fine. And then the game came out in October of 2001. It was gradual all the way through till Christmas 2001 into early 2002, and it just didn't stop selling. It's not like any single week was that massive. It was that every week it just rumbled on." The art he's referring to (above) is, of course, as iconic as the staples of GTA 3's newly-open world gameplay. Houser notes this, and reflects: "GTA has become part of the wider cultural fabric. I mean, you sort of saw that on YouTube clips and whatever else that would have the HUD on it, and people using the logo and things like that. When you go to any big tourist resort, you'll have a sort of GTA cover art-inspired T-shirt available. So you began to see that creep in 10 years ago." This isn't the first we've heard from Dan Houser in the past few months. Back in July, the Rockstar Games co-founder joined longtime GTA writer Lazlow Jones to espouse some opinions on the on-going physical games debate . "I don't know that I care," he responded when asked about the fact that Sony plans to scrap physical discs from January 20-28 onwards, "but if people want that, companies should provide it. I think the ability to update games - as critical as people are on digital releases - the ability to update and fix problems in games have been very useful to the quality of games." Elsewhere, with his company Absurd Ventures, Houser is working on an " open world action-adventure ". This is the first time we get a look at "just a few characters" coming to a "story-driven action-comedy adventure game set in the Absurdaverse".

sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: GTA 6 is ‘Never Completed Settled’, Rockstar Reveals
sources.text: In a new interview, Rockstar’s head of development discussed how GTA 6 is never fully settled. GTA 6 is all set to release in just over a month, and fans still can’t believe that the game is so close. Leading up to the launch, Rockstar has given players insights into what went into developing a title of this scale and has also touched on the delays it faced, none of which were for any dramatic reason. In a recent interview with Bloomberg , Phil Hooker, Rockstar’s head of development, stated that GTA 6 is never fully settled. He said the game’s delays have never been due to major, dramatic issues; instead, they result from elements not coming together as planned within the intended timeframe. Hooker also noted that the team doesn’t follow a strict blueprint for the game’s development and has changed things even “within the last few months.” Hooker also pointed out that Rockstar built a new studio in Los Angeles to focus solely on creating NPCs. Hooker talked about playing a version of the game that was meant to lead him to a story mission but took an unexpected turn. Instead, he collided with a car, resolved the situation peacefully, and then visited a convenience store to pick up items to restore his health. Later, Hooker had a violent encounter with an NPC who insulted him and also robbed a store while the counter was unattended. He was then chased by the cops and managed to escape by ditching his car and finding a new one. Realizing that the new vehicle could be sold for a pretty penny, he attempted to sell it. On his way, another car blasting loud music rammed into him. He pursued the car and discovered a compound filled with more goods to fence. Hooker explained that two hours into their session, he still hadn’t even come close to completing the story mission. What are your thoughts on GTA 6 never being completely settled? sources.title: Rumor: Grand Theft Auto VI coming to PC in Q1 2027
sources.text: Rockstar Games plans to release a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI within the first three months of 2027, according to a GamesBeat report citing “four industry sources familiar with the studio’s plans.” Grand Theft Auto VI is due out for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on November 19, meaning the PC release would arrive no more than four months after its console launch. The previous iteration of the series, Grand Theft Auto V , did not arrive on PC until roughly one year and seven months after its initial release. And Rockstar Games’ latest major new title, Red Dead Redemption 2 , took just over a year to come to PC. Rockstar Games did not respond to GamesBeat’s request for comment.

sources.title: REPLACED coming to Android on December 8
sources.text: Publisher Atari and developer Sad Cat Studios will release atmospheric narrative-driven cyberpunk adventure game REPLACED for Android via Google Play on December 8, the companies announced. REPLACED first launched for Xbox Series and PC via Steam , Epic Games Store , Microsoft Store , and GOG on April 14. It is also available via Game Pass. Here is an overview of the game, via Atari: The mobile version is part of the Google Play Games program, offering seamless gaming across mobile, tablets, and PC via a single purchase. The Android version, ported by Poland-based studio The Knights of U, will allow a new audience to experience the same jaw-dropping cinematic visuals and immersive atmosphere that those players loved on its original PC and console release. REPLACED has been played by over 900,000 players across all platforms since its release in Spring 2026. REPLACED is a narrative-driven 2.5D platformer blending cinematic exploration with fluid, free-flow action. Immerse yourself in an alternate 1980s America reshaped by nuclear catastrophe and meet the downtrodden of Phoenix City as you struggle to survive. Soak up the game’s rich atmosphere as you walk the streets of Phoenix-City and become a part of the stories of the citizens you meet in this dark cyberpunk thriller. As you uncover the sinister secrets of Phoenix Corporation, REPLACED explores themes of humanity, identity, and control through morally complex characters and the slow reveal of a world pushed to its limits. Discover a haven for corruption where outlaws thrive and human life is traded like currency as R.E.A.C.H.—an AI trapped in a human body against its will. Expose the Corporation’s hidden agenda, and uncover the purpose behind your creation in a world where every secret—and every life—has a price.

stories.title: Sifu chega ao Android e iOS com combate de kung-fu adaptado para celulares
stories.summary: Jogo de ação lançado originalmente em 2022 ganha versão mobile com controles de toque, câmera adaptativa e mecânicas de combate preservadas O post Sifu chega ao Android e iOS com combate de kung-fu adaptado para celulares apareceu primeiro em Olhar Digital .

sources.name: Olhar Digital Games
sources.title: Sifu chega ao Android e iOS com combate de kung-fu adaptado para celulares
sources.text: Sifu , jogo de ação e artes marciais desenvolvido pela Sloclap, já está disponível para dispositivos Android e iOS . Lançada nesta terça-feira (13), a versão mobile adapta a experiência original de 2022 para telas menores, com mudanças nos controles e na câmera. O título mantém sua proposta de combate baseado em kung-fu, no qual os jogadores precisam dominar técnicas de defesa, contra-ataques e combinações de golpes para superar os adversários. A principal novidade está na adaptação da jogabilidade para smartphones. A versão mobile apresenta controles de toque desenvolvidos para preservar a precisão e a intensidade dos confrontos. O jogo também conta com interações com o ambiente simplificadas e uma câmera adaptativa, projetada para facilitar a visualização das lutas em telas menores. Segundo a divulgação, o estilo artístico inspirado em pinturas feitas à mão e a apresentação cinematográfica foram mantidos, buscando oferecer uma experiência visual semelhante à das versões anteriores. Ambientado em uma cidade chinesa fictícia, Sifu acompanha um jovem praticante de artes marciais que testemunha o assassinato do pai. Após oito anos de treinamento, ele inicia uma jornada de vingança contra os responsáveis. A jogabilidade combina elementos de roguelike e beat ‘em up, incentivando o aprendizado por meio de tentativas, erros e aperfeiçoamento das técnicas de combate. Para avançar, os jogadores precisam dominar o estilo de kung-fu Pak Mei, identificar as fraquezas dos inimigos e utilizar o ambiente durante os confrontos. Desenvolvido pelo estúdio francês Sloclap, também responsável por Absolver, Sifu chegou originalmente ao mercado em 2022 e agora amplia sua disponibilidade para dispositivos móveis. A versão para Android e iOS já está disponível. Rachele Victoria é formada em Letras, MBA em Inovação e atua há 10 anos com comunicação e conteúdo gamer. Amazon Prime também é feito para jogadores! Todo mês, obtenha itens exclusivos, jogos grátis, uma assinatura gratuita na Twitch.tv e muito mais com sua assinatura Prime . Clique aqui para um teste gratuito de 30 dias .

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Sifu, the singular kung fu action game, is out now on Android and iOS
sources.text: Sifu , Sloclap's 2022 martial arts action game, can now be played on smartphones. The French developer released the game today on Android and iOS , following an announcement earlier in the month. This portable version of Sifu is priced $8 / £6, and the studio said it has been developed specifically for phone screens. The game has new touch-based controls, as you might imagine, which translate its core moves to on-screen prompts, with environmental interactions streamlined. The ports also have a new, adaptive camera which Sloclap said works better on smaller screens. The developer said it worked to retain Sifu's painterly look, and its fluid and impactful combat for the mobile release, but the game also supports controllers if you prefer. Judging by the trailer, it does look like the Sifu we know, albeit with a softer image as a result of the less powerful hardware. Sifu was critically acclaimed and sold 1 million copies in its first three weeks of release . Previously a PlayStation and Epic Games Store exclusive, Sifu made its way to Steam and Xbox a year later . Sloclap followed Sifu with something altogether different: a third-person football game called Rematch. The game is likewise critically acclaimed and commercially successful , but its reveal left fans who were eager for a sequel to Sifu disappointed . While Sloclap continues to support Rematch, the studio's future plans remain unknown. Sloclap's three developed games are all notably distinct. The studio's debut title, Absolver, is a martial arts MMO. Then came Sifu, a single-player kung fu game, which was followed up by a third-person football game in Rematch. It's anyone's guess what genre the studio is going to tackle next.
